# Validation fixture

Everything needed to reproduce the validation of `imap_forensic_collector.py`
against a known mailbox on a real IMAP server, and to compare your result with
the recorded one.

## Contents

| path | what it is |
|---|---|
| `dovecot-maildir-tester.tar.gz` | The raw mailbox exactly as stored by the Dovecot test server: Maildir for user `tester`, 8 folders, 96 messages. Includes each folder's `dovecot-uidlist` (carries UIDVALIDITY and every UID assignment) and Dovecot index files. File mtimes inside the tarball are the messages' INTERNALDATE; Maildir filename suffixes are the flags. Restoring this reproduces the mailbox byte-for-byte including UIDs. |
| `config.validation.ini` | The collector configuration used to produce `expected/`. |
| `expected/` | The collector's output from a run against that mailbox: `manifest.csv`, `manifest.sha256`, `collection.log`, and `mail/<folder>/<uid>.eml` (96 files). |
| `../docker/docker-compose.yml`, `dovecot.conf`, `users` | The server definition. User `tester`, password `testpass`, IMAP over TLS on `127.0.0.1:9993`, `.` hierarchy delimiter with `INBOX.` prefix (same layout as OpenSRS/hostedemail). |
| `../docker/seed_mailbox.py` | How the mailbox content was originally generated (IMAP `CREATE`/`APPEND`). Kept for provenance; **do not use it to reproduce** — it assigns fresh UIDs and INTERNALDATEs every run. Use the tarball. |
| `../docker/export_mailbox.py`, `restore_mailbox.py` | Copy the Maildir out of / into the container. |
| `../tests/compare_collections.py` | Compares two collections message-by-message. |

The TLS certificate is *not* part of the fixture. It is self-signed and generated on
first `docker compose up`; the collector logs its CN, expiry, and the CA file's SHA-256
in the header of every run, so a different certificate is expected and visible.

## What the mailbox contains

Generated by `seed_mailbox.py` (seeded RNG, so flag/date choices were deterministic;
UIDs came from the server). 12 messages in each of:

```
INBOX
INBOX.Sent                          (\Sent special-use)
INBOX.Drafts                        (\Drafts special-use)
INBOX.Archive
INBOX.Archive.2019                  nested
INBOX.Archive.2019.Q4 Invoices      nested, space in name
INBOX.ältere Projekte               non-ASCII name (modified UTF-7 on the wire: &AOQ-ltere Projekte)
INBOX.Clients.Smith & Co            '&' in name (on the wire: &-); parent INBOX.Clients is \Noselect
```

Messages include RFC 2047 base64 (UTF-8) and quoted-printable (ISO-8859-1) subjects,
a subject with raw un-encoded UTF-8, roughly half flagged `\Seen`, some `\Flagged`,
INTERNALDATEs spread over three years, and every seventh message deliberately
malformed: no `Message-ID`, bare-LF line endings, raw `0xFF 0xFE` bytes.

## Reproducing the validation

Requires Docker Desktop and Python 3.11+. From the repository root:

```powershell
# 1. Start a clean server (discards any previous test mailbox)
cd docker
docker compose down -v
docker compose up -d
cd ..

# 2. Load the fixture mailbox into it
python docker\restore_mailbox.py

# 3. Collect
$env:IMAP_PASSWORD = 'testpass'
python imap_forensic_collector.py --config testdata\config.validation.ini --output my_run
python imap_forensic_collector.py --config testdata\config.validation.ini --output my_run --verify-only

# 4. Compare with the recorded result
python tests\compare_collections.py testdata\expected my_run
```

Expected: the collector footer reports `Completeness check: PASS` for 96 messages,
`--verify-only` reports `VERIFY RESULT: PASS`, and the comparison ends with
`compared 96 message(s) ... problems=0` / `RESULT: MATCH`.

The comparison is on `sha256`, `size_bytes`, `internaldate_utc`, `flags`,
`message_id`, `subject`, and the on-disk hash of each `.eml`, keyed by
`(folder, uidvalidity, uid)`. The `\Recent` flag is ignored because it is
per-session server state, not a property of the message.

Things that legitimately differ between your run and `expected/collection.log`:
timestamps, elapsed time, hostname, Python version and path, output path, and the
TLS certificate details. `manifest.csv` should be identical except for the
`relative_path` column if you chose a different output directory name, and
possibly `\Recent` in `flags`.

## Additional checks you can repeat

- **Server not modified:** snapshot every folder's flags with a read-only client
  before and after the collection (`EXAMINE` + `UID FETCH 1:* (FLAGS)`); they must be
  identical. In particular unread messages must stay unread.
- **Resume:** kill the collector mid-run (`Ctrl+C` or task kill), re-run with
  `--resume`, then `--verify-only` and the comparison above. No duplicates, no gaps.
- **UIDVALIDITY change:** delete and recreate a folder on the test server, then
  `--resume`; the folder must be re-collected into `<dir>__uidvalidity<N>` with an
  ERROR in the log.

## Regenerating the fixture

Only if the fixture itself needs to change. Record the reason in the commit.

```powershell
cd docker; docker compose down -v; docker compose up -d
python seed_mailbox.py            # or any other method of populating the mailbox
python export_mailbox.py          # -> testdata/dovecot-maildir-tester.tar.gz
cd ..
Remove-Item -Recurse testdata\expected
$env:IMAP_PASSWORD = 'testpass'
python imap_forensic_collector.py --config testdata\config.validation.ini
python imap_forensic_collector.py --config testdata\config.validation.ini --verify-only
```
